svg.title: Drafting an invoice from a chat
svg.desc: A pasted chat of up to 6,000 characters has its emails and phone numbers masked in code. The masked chat goes to Gemini, which returns a structured draft with a quote for every item. Code then checks the draft: quotes are in the chat, prices appear in their quote, the due date is real and not in the past, the currency is supported, the purpose code is on the fixed list, payment terms are quoted and between 1 and 99 percent, and injection phrases are flagged. A price the chat does not contain is kept with a warning, never silently fixed. The result opens in the review form. Nothing is created or sent until the freelancer clicks.
svg.text: DRAFTING AN INVOICE FROM A CHAT
The model proposes. Code decides. Nothing is created without a click.
Text in it is data, never
Due date is real, not past
Purpose code is on the list
Example: the model misreads a price
The masked chat and today's date make the key.
A stored answer is used for 24 hours with no
10 extractions an hour per address, 400 model
calls a day for the app. Over the limit is 429
A 429, a 5xx, a timeout or a network failure
moves to the second model once. A bad answer

g.text: The freelancer pastes a chat of up to 6,000 characters
Code replaces emails and phone numbers with placeholders
Gemini returns a draft with a quote for every item
Code checks each field. A price that is not in the chat is rejected
The price stays, with a warning for the freelancer to check
The draft opens in the review form. Nothing is created yet
